sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed for N-terminally tagged CysLT2R constructs (L4: receptor surface expression in Sf9 cells confirmed for the FLAG-bearing crystallography construct). In the same publication (PMC7948404), the closely related CysLTR2-GFP10 (C-terminal tag) construct showed dose-dependent IP1 accumulation in response to LTD4, confirming the receptor is functional when tagged; the N-terminal FLAG construct's functional result is not explicitly reported in the ledger clips.
sites.rationale: CysLT2R (UniProt Q9NS75) has no annotated signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–42 as extracellular, making the N-terminus the sole extracellular terminus of the receptor. A tag prepended before M1 (insert_after_residue = 0) sits 43 residues from the TM1 boundary (residue 43), well clear of the ≥3-residue constraint. The position is topology_derived because no ledger clip names a specific residue number for the junction, but with a single extracellular terminus and no signal peptide there is exactly one possible location. Four independent ledger lines (L3, L5, L11, L12) across two publications all place a FLAG tag at the N-terminus of full-length, membrane-anchored CysLT2R, providing strong convergent support. Human CysLTR2 cloned into pcDNA3.1(+) with an N-terminal FLAG tag (DYKDDDDK) and a C-terminal 1D4 epitope tag, creating a doubly-tagged full-length receptor construct expressed in HEK293T cells. The same N-terminal FLAG arrangement is independently reported in at least three additional constructs (L3, L11, L12) across two publications.

sources.claim: The synthetic vector encodes human CysLTR2 cDNA in pcDNA3.1(+) fused to an N-terminal FLAG tag (DYKDDDDK) and a C-terminal 1D4 epitope tag (TETSQVAPA) ( 2 ).

literature_notes: L1 and L2 report BRIL insertion into ICL3 (between E232 and V240); ICL3 spans residues 226–245 (intracellular) — not a surface site, recorded in other_positions. L6, L7, L8 report C-terminal GFP10 fusions; the C-terminus falls in the intracellular span 308–346 — not a surface site, recorded in other_positions (L8 confirms function is preserved for this intracellular tag). L9 and L10 describe structural constructs with C-terminal NanoBiT and N-terminal BRIL fusions used for cryo-EM; the BRIL at the N-terminus in L10 is a large fusion protein for structure determination rather than a short epitope tag, and the construct carries additional truncations and mutations that preclude treating it as an independent validation of a surface tag site — it is subsumed by the stronger FLAG evidence. L11 also carries a C-terminal 8×His tag (intracellular) noted in other_positions. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop (ECL1 94–123, ECL2 175–204, ECL3 267–286) insertion for CysLT2R.

literature_other_positions.note: BRIL inserted between E232 and V240 in ICL3 (intracellular span 226–245) for crystallography; tolerated but faces the cytoplasm.

C-terminal GFP10 fusion after the last residue (V346) in the intracellular C-tail (308–346); functional — dose-dependent IP1 accumulation in response to LTD4 confirmed in HEK293T cells — but not a surface site.
C-terminal 1D4 epitope tag (TETSQVAPA) appended after V346 in the intracellular C-tail; tolerated but faces the cytoplasm.
